newsitem.title: USA: NY Fed chief says G10 to monitor electronic money.
newsitem.headline: NY Fed chief says G10 to monitor electronic money.

text.p: The advent of electronic money may not create significant problems for policymakers in the near term, but will need to be monitored, New York Federal Reserve Bank President William McDonough said Thursday.

"While electronic money may not create significant problems for public policy in the very near future, it will be important to monitor developments and share information internationally," McDonough said in prepared remarks to a Treasury Department conference on electronic money.
He said the focus of the Group of 10 industrial nations' central banks will be on the need to fully understand and continuously monitor the development of these new products.
"Acting in advance of a full understanding entails a substantial risk that government will stifle potentially important innovation in the high technology private sector," he added.
